title.title: A doubling subset of Hilbert space that fits in no $\mathbb{R}^k$
title.subtitle: Claim: a subset of $\ell_2$ with doubling constant at most 76,800 has no bi-Lipschitz embedding into any $\mathbb{R}^k$

plain: A shape that looks finite-dimensional at every zoom level, yet fits faithfully into no finite space

object.caption: schematic: a base plane with coloured strips, at one of many sparse scales

beats.text: Doubling: every ball is covered by boundedly many balls of half the radius
The set stacks orthogonal displacements over a plane, steered by coloured strips
Claim: any map into some $\mathbb{R}^k$ crowds too many separated points into a ball

steps: Start from a plane; lift points in new perpendicular directions
Coloured strips at sparse scales decide where each lift goes
Any map into $\mathbb{R}^k$ would crowd too many points into a ball

achievement.label: Question of Lang and Plaut (2001)
achievement.context: Answer: no. A subset of $\ell_2$ with doubling constant at most 76,800 embeds in no $\mathbb{R}^k$
achievement.note: Before: counterexamples only in $L_p$, $p>2$; a 2017 Hilbert attempt was withdrawn

verify.detail: In Lean: the $\ell_2$ set, and a compact one in every infinite-dimensional Banach space
verify.ourCheck: From the paper and its Lean docs; we did not build the Lean

voice.text: Doubling: every ball is covered by few half-size balls. Surely such sets fit somewhere finite?
Stack perpendicular lifts on a plane; any embedding then crowds too many points.
Claimed: no embedding, at any distortion.

sources.quote: There is a fixed subset S of real l_2 with doubling constant at most 76800 that admits no bi-Lipschitz embedding into any R^k at any finite distortion.
Lang and Plaut (Geom. Dedicata 87, 2001, Question 2.4) asked whether every doubling subset of Hilbert space bi-Lipschitz embeds in some R^k
Schioppa's 2017 claimed Hilbert counterexample (arXiv:1703.10265) was withdrawn.
Lafforgue-Naor (Geom. Dedicata 172, 2014) gave a counterexample in L_p for p>2
The construction stacks orthogonal displacements on a base plane, controlled by periodically coloured horizontal and vertical strips at sparse scales.

sources.ref: article, A doubling subset of Hilbert space
sources.quote: Differentiating a would-be embedding on "sheets" forces too many separated points into a bounded ball.
